sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.11)
sections.text: Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Directorate Control Directorate Controller: Drs. Lieutenant Commander (kltz) P.J. van Roon CPC, from September 1 Lieutenant Commander (kltz) C.M. van der Pijl MMO EMSD The staff department Directorate Control consists of a Management Information office and a Financial Control office and is formally under F&C CZSK. Management Information The vision of CZMCARIB has been revised: “CZMCARIB is the relevant maritime and security partner in the Caribbean, as part of CZSK.” In line with this, the Annual Plan CZMCARIB has been established. Throughout the year, we prepared quarterly reports for accountability towards CZSK and for internal steering within CZMCARIB. The performance indicators prescribed by CZSK have been supplemented with our own internal indicators. These have been secured in the ‘Brugpaneel CZMCARIB’ which was officially put into use this year. Additionally, we mapped and secured the operations at CZMCARIB through process descriptions. The year was also marked by the optimization of SAP M&F and the implementation of Assortimentsgewijs Werken in de West (AGWW). Finally, we further developed SharePoint CZMCARIB, which is now widely used within the CARIB organization. Finances As of January 1, the payment office CZMCARIB and several financial management tasks were formally transferred to the Financial Administration and Management Office (FABK) of the Facilities and Logistics division of the Defense Support Command. The reallocation of financial management tasks to the FABK meant that CZMCARIB no longer performs accounting tasks, prior oversight of intended expenditures, and accountability for invoice payments. Consequently, four positions with the military personnel assigned to them were transferred to the FABK. Due to an increasingly intensive use of SAP M&F, including Assortimentsgewijs werken and VAM, it became apparent that traditional budget positions were underperforming and there was an unbudgeted realization associated with the budget position linked to SAP M&F. In 2017, based on financial volume, approximately 8% of the total realization of CZMCARIB was made payable through SAP M&F. The emergency aid resulting from the passage of Hurricane Irma in the Windward Islands resulted in €0.8 million in unbudgeted items. These additional expenditures were submitted to the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations and subsequently reconciled with CZMCARIB. In total, the final realization of CZMCARIB amounted to €20.5 million, thus remaining within the allocated budget.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.12)
sections.text: 7_Navy_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-12 197 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Base Marine Base Parera (MBPAR) Commander: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) E.G.J. Hekkers General The motto accompanying the emblem of Marine Base Parera (MBPAR) is 'o pgewekt en vrijmoedig' (awakened and bold). Two character traits that are characteristic of a good 'host'. A large part of the year, the company restaurant 'Lamunchi' was under renovation, which was completed in November. The restaurant meets the latest standards and techniques, ensuring it will serve well for years to come. This beautiful result was thanks to intensive and good cooperation between the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf, the works council (as initiator), and the Logistics Service Food (LDV) staff of MBPAR. Additionally, the new Rima pier was completed and gratefully put into use by the support ship Zr.Ms. Pelikaan and the various station ships. The return of the 'West Ship' to the base has also restored the old robust military appearance of Parera, with all military units centralized at the military locations on the island. As part of maintenance, painting work and replacement of air conditioning units took place. There was also a cleanup of the so-called 'peanut butter area', where this year, through auctions/sales, more clarity has been achieved. The area is now organized, and all objects have been identified. Support and Assistance For Parera, the autumn was largely focused on providing assistance to the Leeward Islands after Hurricane Irma. Curaçao served during this period as a logistical transit point between the Netherlands and the Leeward Islands. The capacity of Parera was maximally utilized, with the sleeping accommodations (regularly 204 beds and 40 (emergency) sleeping places in the sports hall) being fully occupied, requiring daily food supplies for the entire occupancy. In addition to preparing meals at the base itself, mobile field kitchens, with LDV personnel from MBPAR, were deployed on Sint Maarten to support the military troops there. The MB-

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.13)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean PAR personnel proudly reflects on the support provided for delivering emergency aid. Additionally, MBPAR supported events throughout the year such as King's Day, the KLM Marathon, Tech Triathlon, Christmas Eve celebration, and the Christmas Market at Landhuis Ascension. The latter is a grand Christmas market at the Landhuis on the western side of Curaçao. CZMCARIB also made itself visible on this side of the island and provided a beautiful Christmas event for the local population and its own personnel. Accommodation The accommodation has a spacious capacity for sleeping places, of which more than half is allocated to the KL Company in the West. The remaining places are used by boarders/sleep-in personnel, visiting units, and business travelers. Throughout the year, the accommodation was occupied for more than 90%, and during the deployment for emergency aid to Sint Maarten, even above 100% by creating emergency sleeping accommodation in the Sports Hall. Finally, the barracks prepared this year for improvements to the E-welfare in the sleeping accommodations and day rooms. In 2018, the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf will begin with the Zr.Ms. Zeeland en route from Curaçao to Sint Maarten.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.14)
sections.text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied is working on the installation of a new internet cable that can deliver data speeds up to modern standards. Digital television, fast (data) communication, and online gaming are expected to take shape in 2018 for all guests at the base. FT&S Development & Recreation (O&O) Like in previous years, FT&S organized many activities outside of regular sports support. Examples include the KLM marathon, the MTB tours, the Kingdom Games, the indoor football tournament, the team-building sports day, and activities for children (such as the Sinterklaas celebration, children's parties at the swimming pool, and Halloween kids movie night). The sports conditions in Curaçao remain optimal with two sports halls (MKSUF and MBPAR) and a swimming pool. Additionally, the barracks leadership decided last year to add a climbing tower, which was a strong desire of a large part of the staff, allowing climbing skills to be well maintained in the Caribbean. Company Restaurant The renovation of the company restaurant took place this year and was completed to full satisfaction in November. The official opening will take place in early 2018. During the period when the restaurant was unavailable, meals were prepared from mobile Karcher units of the Defense Loan Organization near the longroom for onboard placers/overnighters from MBPAR. The LDV staff managed to provide a warm meal daily from these less than optimal circumstances that met the quality standards expected of a regular company restaurant. Administration In December, the Administration Office was merged with the Defense International Support Service Center (DCIOD) into a joint support point/one-stop shop as part of the "Reorganization International Support Caribbean" project. This optimizes the organization's service to employees and their families.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.15)
sections.text: 7_Navy_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-15 200 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Marine Barracks Suffisant (MKSUF) Commander: Major (majmarns) C.E. Arriëns Dwarshuis, from February 27 Major (majmarns) C. van Dinteren The Marine Barracks Suffisant (MKSUF) was responsible this year for the readiness of CURMIL, continued the initiated movement towards the professionalization of this unit, welcomed the establishment of the Training Center CARIB, executed its facilitating role for visiting training units, and remained responsible for carrying out the Social Formation Trajectory (SVT). The support for the emergency relief operation following hurricanes Irma, Jose, and Maria demanded the utmost from the barracks and its crew. MKSUF committed to supporting, transporting, and registering refugees at Hato Airport. The barracks also facilitated the accommodation of many hundreds of military personnel participating in the emergency relief efforts. Even during the re-deployment, MKSUF was the location used by units before flying back to the Netherlands. A large number of discussions regarding collegial networking were held at the barracks. Throughout the year, training units from the Netherlands found their way to the barracks; military personnel participated in the exercise Daktari, NLMARSOF, DDG, KWCARIB, the MOC, and the sniper training. Foreign units, such as a French unit from Martinique, were also accommodated and supported in their training. This year, the MKSUF/Training department became a formal school of OKM under the name OCC. In terms of size, the largest Basic Military Training (EMV) in recent years started in September. The preparations for setting up and executing (information, recruitment, assessments, equipment arrangements) required significant effort from the crew in the spring, ultimately leading to a successful EMV start in September with 67 trainees. Training For years, MKSUF has been active in training young people from Curaçao and Aruba who see their future in the militias of both countries. The OCC prepares, organizes, and conducts three career training programs for Caribbean Militias (CARMIL). The VVO, which started in 2016, saw fourteen trainees from both Curaçao and Aruba ultimately earn the rank insignia of corporal. Additionally, two officer training programs (PO-

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.16)
sections.text: 7_KM_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-16 201 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Area TOC) were on the agenda. After a pre-selection (Pre-POTOC), two Aruban candidates who started in 2016 were allowed to travel to the Netherlands in the spring. In August, a candidate from Curaçao began at the MOC in Rotterdam. Because working at CARMIL is not a lifetime employment, the intake and the EMV, quantitatively but especially qualitatively, must be sufficiently robust. Of the 128 candidates, 78 were selected after a fitness test, a medical examination, and a psychological assessment. 67 local boys started, and ultimately 47 candidates completed the first intensive part of the one-year training after 4 months, resulting in a dropout rate of less than 30%, before they began the MBO certified training in Security and Surveillance or the combat training. The green and blue platoon CURMIL The CURMIL green platoon is the operationally deployable unit. The Ministry of Justice and Security frequently requests assistance from Defense in reducing crime on the island. Ta Basta Awor, loosely translated as "Now is Enough," is one of the operations carried out. At the end of 2017, the authority of CURMIL was expanded to include the ability to search vehicles. Not only crime, but also other tensions on the island, such as support for local security services during the December strikes, required additional deployment of CURMIL. The CURMIL deployment for humanitarian aid operations in Sint Maarten, Saba, Sint Eustatius, and Dominica was unique; for the first time, this unit was deployed in such an operation. Their contribution proved to be of great added value to the operation. These troops speak the language, understand the culture, and are the perfect intermediaries between the deployed units and the local population. Through various national and international training programs, CURMIL continuously worked on their readiness and further professionalization, culminating in their successful participation in the French 'Commando' training in Martinique for the first time. Of the eleven candidates, nine CURMIL members successfully completed the training and earned the coveted badge. The social relevance and visibility of CURMIL in Curaçao in the context of maintaining social support received much attention. Charitable actions such as work on the children's care pavilion at the Christian foundation Siloam, organizing and conducting various sports activities for elementary school children, recruitment programs at secondary schools, and support for na-

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.17)
sections.text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied 202 The Command of the Navy in the Caribbean contributed significantly to its visibility through national holidays and participation in various ceremonial tasks. Once a year, a personnel change takes place, and militia members and corporals transition from the green platoon to the blue platoon. This latter platoon, which has been trained in their initial military formation to guard and secure defense objects, is deployed at both the naval base Suffisant and the naval base Parera. The guarding and securing of defense locations in Curaçao by the CURMIL is a responsible task that requires a great deal of discipline and ongoing retraining and IBT training. Social Formation Trajectory (SVT) The SVT is a training trajectory of approximately five months. This trajectory is aimed at instilling a positive behavioral change in underprivileged youth who have, for various reasons, found themselves on the fringes of society. Despite positive discussions with the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture, and Sports in Curaçao and a project group in Amsterdam, the next phase was postponed for budgetary reasons. Marines train in Curaçao.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.18)
sections.text: 7_KM_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-18 203 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Region postponed the SVT appearance to the second half of 2018. Safety and health MKSUF has placed safety high on the agenda, once again as OCC. In mid-2017, both the business emergency plan and the BHV plan were revised, and various enforcement inspections yielded a positive score. In close collaboration with the Health Center Parera, a concept for general practitioner facilities for CURMIL and the Aruban Militia (ARUMIL) was developed, enabling EMV, VVO, and Pre-POTOC candidates to access this care. Beyond emergency assistance, more options were developed to initially secure deployability advice for CURMIL. Marine Barracks Savaneta Aruba (MSKSAV) Commander: Lieutenant Colonel (ltkolmarns) T.A. van Dishoeck Commander 32nd Marine Battalion Major (majmarns) O.L.F. Prins General This year, Marine Barracks Savaneta (MSKSAV) worked well with the staff of CZMCA-RIB to write an ambition document. The barracks, as in previous years, fulfilled the now clearly and concretely formulated mission to be the relevant maritime and security partner for its partners in Aruba. This year, marines were also ready for a potential assistance request in light of the elections that took place on September 22. 32nd Marine Company in the CARIB (MCC)/ 32nd Raiding Squadron (32RSQN) Reorganization MCC The transition from company to raiding squadron occurred this year. This partially aligns this unit with the units in the Netherlands. Compared to them, however, each raiding section lacks a designated marksman and an infantry engineer. As a result, a Troop consists of 28 men instead of 32 as in the Netherlands. However, the same structure as the units within an MCG has been maintained, allowing personnel to adapt more easily within 32RSQN. Military Operations Urban Terrain (MOUT) The 32RSQN, including the ARUMIL, underwent an annual recurring training in the spring of 2017 according to the Three Block War concept. The 32nd conducted this training...

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.19)
sections.text: Command of the Navy in the Caribbean conducted training with two Troops, a FRISC (Fast Raiding Interception and Special Forces Craft) Troop and the staff up to and including level 4+. Various enablers from the Netherlands (Raven and RSTA) were brought in to support this training. The unit trained in a complex spectrum of modern warfare in which they had to switch between full-scale war, peacekeeping, and humanitarian assistance. BVW Training One of the main tasks of 32RSQN is to keep a Troop of Marines permanently ready for the Containment of Disturbances (BVW). To have a unit ready for this, an annual training staff from the Royal Marechaussee is brought in to provide this training. This includes training in the various specializations, levels, and also the cooperation between them. This year, 1-Troop was responsible for carrying out this main task. Exercise Black Horse Since the 13th RSQN started in 2017 with only two Troops instead of the desired three, the decision was made to conduct the exercise Black Horse in the USA (Twente Marine Barracks Savaneta).

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.20)
sections.text:
Commandement of the Navy in the Caribbean

3rd Troop of the 32nd Reconnaissance Squadron (32RSQN) participated. As a result, the 13th Combat Command (CC) operated organically with three troops. The objective of the exercise was to operate with 'combined arms' in a live fire setting. For this, there was support from American tanks and anti-tank units, and from the Netherlands, the 15th Reconnaissance and Surveillance Troop (15e RSTA) and the 14th Combat Support (14e CS) participated in the exercise.

Emergency Aid to Sint Maarten, Saba, and Sint Eustatius

The 32RSQN, including ARUMIL, provided emergency aid in September on the Windward Islands after Hurricane Irma. The unit was already stationed on the islands prior to the passage. The 32RSQN was therefore the first unit to provide both hard and soft military assistance. The 32RSQN undertook the following tasks: staffing emergency shelters before and after the passage; supporting prison security; conducting patrols and setting up checkpoints at vital intersections; securing the air and sea ports to facilitate the transport of both personnel and equipment. Ultimately, the 32RSQN was active in the area for two weeks, after which the Maritime Support Task Unit (MSTU) relieved them.

French Commando Training in Martinique

It is an old tradition for units of the Royal Netherlands Navy Command Caribbean (CZMCARIB) to participate in French commando training in Martinique. This has been conducted in recent years under the name Unit Cohesion Training. The training maintains and strengthens the (strategic) partnership with the French armed forces in the Caribbean. Additionally, the participating units practiced: completing the French jungle training; validating personal physical and mental readiness; improving junior leadership at levels 2 and 3; validating the expeditionary mindset by operating in and under extreme conditions; and intensifying cooperation with the French headquarters in Martinique. The 3rd Troop, ARU, and CURMIL participated in the training. Prior to the start of the training, the 3rd Troop underwent an intensive preparation program and also completed the French and Dutch Jungle tests. The French commando training consists of three components: a jungle component, a maritime component, and the final exercise. Ultimately, 19 marines from the 3rd Troop and 10 ARUMIL participated.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.21)
sections.text:
Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied

In November 2017, under the leadership of the MTC from Doorn, a three-week military tracking training was conducted. The objective of this training was to make the participating personnel skilled in tracking trails in the terrain. Additionally, they used military tracking with a realistic scenario in the training to also practice in a professional context. Six marines from 1-Troop participated in the training. These sailors were also deployed in various assistance requests in November to directly apply their new tracking specialty.

Training Zr.Ms. Karel Doorman

As part of the main task 'ready for deployment for territorial defense', the unit conducted an exercise in November in cooperation with the Joint Support Ship Zr.Ms. Karel Doorman. This collaboration enabled both the ship and the 32RSQN to practice amphibious operations. For 32RSQN, this was the first amphibious training aboard the Joint Support Ship. 1-Troop had a facilitating and training role during the exercise.

Military Assistance

In the autumn, the 32RSQN provided significant assistance at the request of the governor of Aruba with the following support.

Search Operation House (searching for weapons)

A mixed team of search-trained personnel and trackers (10 marines) searched a house in support of an investigation by the detective unit. The task was to find a weapon. The support ensured that the designated property was systematically, thoroughly, and quickly searched. Ultimately, no weapon was found, but the involvement of the search team minimized the burden on the local residents.

Search Operation

In November, 32RSQN, together with ARUMIL, supported the KPA in an urgent search. It concerned a missing person. It was presumed that this individual was a victim of a crime. The 32RSQN provided search capacity that made it possible to search more quickly across different axes. Ultimately, the person was found deceased by the KPA after further investigation.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.22)
sections.text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied Search operation (containers) The 32nd Reconnaissance Squadron (32RSQN) searched five containers at the request of the KPA, in which narcotics were suspected to be hidden. A composite group of infantry engineers, trackers, and logistics personnel, including a mechanic and forklift drivers, carried out this search operation. During this operation, 300 kilograms of cocaine were found. This search was conducted on MS-KSAV to keep the action discreet. The group had the advantage of easily being able to rely on various resources from the barracks. Logistics and equipment For the deployment in Sint Maarten after Hurricane Irma, the LDV from MSKSAV provided a team to cook in the mobile field kitchen. Two teams from Aruba and Curaçao prepared meals daily for over 700 people in two mobile field kitchens. Inspections In 2017, significant progress was made in the area of Monitor Quality Material. The Royal Netherlands Navy (KM) provided assistance with, among others, Zr.Ms. Zeeland.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.23)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean area focused on inventory management, particularly in the area of weapons and ammunition. The audit did not take place this year due to humanitarian deployment following Hurricane Irma in Sint Maarten. The KKW inspection revealed that a number of weapons were no longer permitted to be used. These were urgently replaced with new material. Additionally, a HACCP audit took place in the area of LDV. SAP MSKSAV increasingly relied on SAP and the corresponding Requests for Orders (ATB’s). As the barracks made more use of framework agreements, logistical processes became simpler and progressed more quickly. In 2017, MSKSAV also utilized a SAP consultant. This also led to an increase in the use of SAP. Staff received regular training, and SAP issues were resolved quickly. On December 7, MSKSAV was the first unit to go live with the SAP blanket orders, allowing contracts with suppliers to be processed more quickly and with less administrative burden. Preparations for the renovation of the company restaurant began this year at Zr.Ms. Zeeland at the quay in Sint Maarten.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.24)
sections.text: Command of the Navy in the Caribbean. The renovation itself will take place in 2018. The head chef, together with the manager of the company restaurant and colleagues in Curaçao, prepared the drawings for the emergency kitchen. Thanks to the efforts of the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf, almost all requests regarding the emergency kitchen have been granted, and MSKSAV is confidently looking forward to the renovation. Barracks / General Service / Infrastructure and Security At the beginning of 2017, the Unit of the Week and MBV components were addressed for the entire permanent crew. Staff CZMCARIB raised topics such as safety, integrity, and security. Various components of the Military Basic Skills were also assessed and repeated. In February, the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf ceremonially handed over the key to the new office building to the barracks. In May, the move took place from five old buildings to 53 new and modern workplaces. Since February 1, MSKSAV has also been supporting the Integrated Seizure Team of the Public Prosecution Service (OM). This team aims to seize goods acquired through fraud. The barracks provides a safe, albeit temporary, storage location. On May 1, MSKSAV held the traditional Open Day for the people of Aruba. The 34,000 visitors experienced a very beautiful and intensive day where, in addition to CZMCARIB, other safety partners such as KPA, fire department, customs, Coast Guard, and KMAR were also presented. With the proceeds from the Open Day, the barracks supported two charities; Imeldahof Children's Home and Fundacion Sinami Paso Pa Paso Aruba. Both organizations received an amount of 7,500 Aruban florins. The barracks organized the sports event the Round of Aruba on May 19, attracting more than 750 runners. Competitions were held in several categories. The event received significant media attention. Next year, the 70+ km endurance run will be expanded to include a military component. The new KMAR building 104 was occupied in August. Despite delays in construction work, this move was still able to take place. The old KMAR building suffered from severe leaks, and the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf prioritized the early delivery of the workplaces.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.25)
sections.text: 7_KM_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-25 210 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Marine Support Point Pointe Blanche (MSTPPB) Detachment Commander: Major (majmarns) R. Witteveen General The Marine Support Point Pointe Blanche (MSTPPB) fulfilled the focus established in 2017: 'a robust operational product'. This was achieved by further standardizing the exercise program and improving the robust operational management that had already received much attention in the previous year. Among other things, the leadership revised the operation order of the MSTPPB in the event of a hurricane. The robust operational product for the SSS islands consists of a MARC-4, Maritime Special Operations Capable (MARSOC) certified Raiding Section from the Netherlands, which is supported and/or supplemented by the Fixed Element of Sint Maarten. This robust operational product focuses during the four-month rotation on the task in the area and possible military assistance. Cooperation with strategic partners and security partners on the SSS islands is central to this. Strengthening this partnership and making the available capabilities known is essential. Cooperation In addition to the regular activities of the MSTPPB, there is collaboration with the Sint Maarten Police Corps, the fire department, the ambulance service, and the Sint Maarten Volunteer Corps. The deployment after Hurricane Irma resulted in closer contact with other (security) partners in Sint Maarten. Visibility Before Hurricane Irma, the MSTPPB dedicated one week of each rotation to a charity week. By implementing this, each Rotating Element was visible in the Windward Islands by executing/supporting projects/activities that are of social importance. After the hurricane, the personnel of the MSTPPB made a significant contribution to the Joint Task Force Sint Maarten. This emergency aid resulted in very positive visibility of military personnel in Sint Maarten. Military Assistance Most of the (hard) military assistance involved searches in the prison. This resulted in the seizure of stabbing weapons, drugs, and other prohibited items. During this year, the unit also found a firearm during a search. In addition

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.26)
sections.text:
Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied conducted searches that provided hard military assistance through the deployment of trackers and a drone in search of two missing persons. Thanks to the deployment of the drone, the trackers quickly found the remains of the two missing individuals. 

Observation 
As part of the annual plan, the support base contributed to improving the information position of CZMCARIB by closely observing and reporting on the security situation in the area. The involved military personnel carried out observation exercises on the SSS islands. These exercises were conducted in close consultation with local security partners. The observation skills of the Rotating Element are one of the capabilities that the security partners do not possess, but for which they have a significant need.

Beat the Marines 
On Saturday, December 9, the MSTPPB organized the sports event Beat The Marines for the third time. This celebrated the corps anniversary with an amphibious obstacle course, challenging the security partners to defeat the marines. Due to the presence of more partners than usual on the island after Hurricane Irma, attendance was high.

Support Vessel Zr.Ms. Pelikaan 
Commander: Lieutenant (ltz1) M.E. van der Eerden 
The year began with the annual maintenance period. Several major projects were undertaken to increase operational readiness and minimize the risk of malfunctions. The most notable was the replacement of all external cabling, which had suffered greatly due to Caribbean weather conditions. We concluded the maintenance period with an internal training program. Following the maintenance period, there was a sailing period for the transport of various supplies and vessels between all the islands of the Kingdom. During these weeks, the ship participated in the Open Day of MSKSAV, making it one of the main attractions. After a transit to the Windward Islands of the Kingdom, it...

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.27)
sections.text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied ship St. Johns, Antigua. As a conclusion to these transport weeks, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan laid a number of anchor stones near Saba. These stones were donated by the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM) to the Saba National Parks Foundation (STINAPA) for the protection of the underwater park so that pleasure craft functioning as dive platforms no longer need to anchor. Immediately after the transport weeks, Zr.Ms. Dolfijn visited the Caribbean for, among other things, an exit & re-entry training of the Netherlands Marine Corps Special Operations Forces (NLMARSOF). Zr.Ms. Pelikaan supported this training by serving as a launch platform, safety ship, and logistical base. In between, the ship facilitated the transport of the CIDW to Bonaire. Immediately following the training with NLMARSOF, we were once again deployed for the transport of the CIDW, this time from Bonaire to Aruba for a joint training of CIDW and the 32nd Reconnaissance Squadron (32RSQN). After the CIDW was brought back from Aruba to Curaçao, several weeks of support followed for the Very Shallow Water (VSW) team of the (DDG). During this period, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan unloaded goods at the quay in Sint Maarten.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.28)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean practiced mine-hunting procedures at various depths around the Leeward Islands, with Zr.Ms. Pelikaan serving as a mother ship and diving platform. After returning to Curaçao in mid-June, the transfer of command from the Commander of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean (CZMCARIB) took place. Zr.Ms. Pelikaan supported this by transporting personnel to and from Aruba and by enhancing the ceremony with its presence, with the newly assigned crew on board in parade formation. This was followed by a period of leave and maintenance. Traditionally, part of the crew changed around the summer leave. A new crew composition began a maintenance period, after which the CIDW was transported to and from Bonaire. This sailing period ended with a port visit to Barbados. Already in the lead-up to this port visit, a hurricane was developing in the Atlantic Ocean. Anticipating its possible path, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan was recalled, necessitating the cancellation of the port visit. While en route to Curaçao, it became clear that the path of the hurricane, now named Irma, would very likely affect the Leeward Islands. All units of CZMCARIB prepared for deployment, and Zr.Ms. Pelikaan was loaded with vehicles, food, and various relief supplies destined for the Leewards. As Hurricane Irma approached Sint Maarten, the ship departed for the aforementioned islands. Irma struck Sint Maarten directly, leaving a trail of destruction. Zr.Ms. Pelikaan was the first ship to dock in Philipsburg and provided immediate support by delivering vehicles and relief supplies, including water and fuel, and by functioning as a logistical base. In the following weeks, the ship operated shuttle services to Curaçao to transport more relief troops, vehicles, and goods to Sint Maarten, establishing a schedule in which the vessel docked in Philipsburg and provided support. Additionally, crew members repaired parts of the harbor, assisted with cleanup operations, and offered technical support. During this time, the ship also sailed to Saba and Sint Eustatius to deliver goods and water. By mid-September, a new catastrophic Category 5 hurricane, Maria, approached from a more southerly direction. This hurricane passed directly over Dominica and left

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.29)
sections.text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied also left a trail of destruction there. From Sint Maarten, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, following Zr.Ms. Zeeland, received a retasking to provide support to Dominica. There followed a period in which the ship and her crew shuttled between various nearby logistical hubs and Dominica to pick up relief supplies. Several times, Roseau, Dominica was visited to deliver the relief supplies to a depot of the World Food Program. Even now, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan provided food and fuel to aid organizations, crew members repaired buildings, and they assisted with cleanup operations. Additionally, the carried FRISC distributed relief supplies directly to affected villages along the coast. After a period of six weeks of continuous deployment, a unique occurrence in the ship's history, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan returned to her home port of Willemstad. Following this intensive period, a compensatory week was observed, followed by several weeks in port to carry out maintenance among other tasks. At the beginning of November, the ship departed for a second period of transport weeks, during which Pelikaan again visited Sint Maarten. The ship also visited St. Johns, Antigua. After completing this period, the ship carried out the remaining part of the year transporting the CIDW to and from Bonaire. Additionally, it supported the MOC by facilitating reconnaissance/snipers with maritime sniping. As a conclusion for the leave, the DDS utilized the ship and crew to support the training of divers. Department of Material Maintenance Head: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) D. van den Bosch, MSc MA Organization & Tasks The Department of Material Maintenance (MI) is responsible for the maintenance and management of equipment, including vehicles, vessels, shore (communication) systems, and other operational resources such as weapons and ammunition under CZMCARIB and the Director KWCARIB. Additionally, MI is also responsible for transport support and all logistical processes. Finally, the MI department is tasked with acquiring and providing equipment and services as well as local disposal. The organization consists of three offices: Technical Support (TO), Logistics & Transport (L&T), and Procurement.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.30)
sections.text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied SAP Operations The implementation of SAP operations was prioritized in 2017 with various supporting visits from colleagues of CZSK/BVIV. The foundation is still not fully in order, although clear improvements are noticeable. In 2018, a SAP evaluation is planned, from which conclusions will be drawn on how to improve operations. Zr.Ms. Pelikaan The support ship with transport capacity underwent a Scheduled Maintenance (BO) in the first period of the year, as usual. This was fully carried out alongside the Rima dock at MBPAR. This year, two major tasks were additionally performed, which could not be postponed until the Maintenance Program scheduled for 2020. The first project involved nearly completely overhauling the hydraulic crane. The second project was the replacement of all external cabling and fixtures. Both projects were completed satisfactorily within the set time and budget. FRISC CZMCARIB has ten FRISC vessels at its disposal. Additionally, there are four FRISCs for the CARIB in the Netherlands that required extensive maintenance from the supplier. At the end of 2017, two arrived, with the remainder arriving in early 2018. The availability of the FRISCs improved significantly compared to previous years. Unfortunately, Hurricane Irma damaged both FRISCs in Sint Maarten to such an extent that they require a lengthy repair process. Coast Guard CARIB KWCARIB has ten super Rigid Hulled Inflatable Boats (RHIB). They have reached the end of their technical lifespan and these vessels will be replaced by Metal Sharks. Unfortunately, the project has been delayed, resulting in delivery now expected in 2018. In addition to the FRISCs in Sint Maarten, two super RHIBs were also severely damaged by Hurricane Irma; these will not be repaired. This year, as planned, a cutter underwent a periodic docking in Suriname, completed with a maintenance period by Materiële Instandhouding Caribisch Gebied (MICAR) in Parera. The other cutters underwent their scheduled maintenance period regularly in Curaçao.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.31)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean 2017 was the first year in which the teething problems of the boats significantly decreased. Remaining issues from new construction have been resolved. Additionally, in 2017, all four boats were included in a regular maintenance cycle for the first time. SEWACO systems The beam path communication system further degraded in 2017. The replacement plan provides for alternative systems in accordance with project JIVC.003 “Securing MULAN service provision in the CARIB,” which is scheduled for 2018. The telephone exchange also further degraded in 2017, severely disrupting internal communication. Replacement is planned for summer 2018. Logistics & Transport The Logistics & Transport (L&T) department has the operational capacity to support the logistical activities of the units, such as (strategic) movements of equipment and personnel. This applies to both the own units of CZMCARIB and visiting national and international units. The department is also responsible for the supply of all units of CZMCARIB and the management and maintenance of all vehicles within CZMCARIB. SAR helicopter of the Coast Guard in Curaçao.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.32)
sections.text:
Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Mid-2017 saw the introduction of 33 new trucks of the IVECO brand in the CARIB to replace the DAFs in Curaçao and Aruba. Although the introduction required significant effort (including retraining drivers, setting up maintenance), these vehicles proved their utility during the emergency assistance after Hurricane Irma. Eight vehicles were deployed for supply activities in Sint Maarten for an extended period without any significant issues. In 2019, the current 40 vehicles of the MB 280cdi type will be replaced by another type of vehicle; the MBs will be transferred to the CLAS. A budget will be allocated for this, which will be used to acquire a replacement. There are opportunities to acquire other vehicles within the developed vehicle plan that are better suited for the CARIB.

Procurement The Procurement department carries out purchasing activities for the maintenance of material (parts, repairs, maintenance) as well as tenders concerning facility services (cleaning, pest control, insurance, residential security, welfare activities, etc.). This applies to both the KWCARIB and, since mid-2017, also to the KMAR CARIB. With the further embedding of the AGWW, the procurement activities are oriented across the entire organization. This allows the organization to work in an overarching manner.

Personnel & Organization Advice Senior P&O advisor: Lt. Commander (ltz1) ing. A.C.F. Melaet For 2017, P&O advice CARIB adhered to the objective of P&O: to provide the organization with sufficient, well-qualified, and motivated personnel. Timely and active staffing policy, good consultation with line managers and P&O CZSK, and a critical view on qualifications have proven essential to place the right employee in the right position. The emergency assistance in Sint Maarten after Irma highlighted the importance of this, concluding that within the small organization of CZM-CARIB and the great distance to the Netherlands, being trained in a timely manner before departure is repeatedly crucial. For P&O advice CARIB, Irma meant a complete halt to regular operations and integration into the N1 structure of the MHKC.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.33)
sections.text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied The collaboration with the HR staff of Caribbean personnel expanded further in 2017 to gain better insight into the shared issues of shortages and to meet the current and future personnel needs. This was to secure knowledge within the CARIB personnel. The strength of the joint deployment of defense personnel, CARMIL (Caribbean Militias; ARU and CURMIL), civil servants, and local officials during the deployment of Irma underscored this need for further collaboration. Nevertheless, it remained difficult to support each other in personnel needs. As in previous years, various career counselors from the LBB P&O CZSK department made a working visit to CZMCARIB in 2017. The career counselors primarily spoke with military personnel who would be repatriating to the Netherlands in 2018. The discussions aimed to provide this group with more clarity about their future opportunities. HRM Caribbean Personnel Staff Officer Local Personnel: Lieutenant (ltz) 2OC C.E. van der Eerden-Borsboom The common thread for 2017 was to bring to the agenda and secure the target group of Caribbean personnel in the (existing) consultation forums CZMCARIB and the defense organization. This created greater awareness of both militias and significant progress was made in organizing the basics. The total training needs and those offered in the budgeting and training systems, labor qualification lists, and job descriptions were updated, and digital personnel files were created. Furthermore, the department developed a compensation scheme for deployment, not being an exercise, and an outplacement trajectory (including a personal exit plan). The (amended) assessment scheme for Curaçao was implemented after several training sessions for supervisors and employees. In this context, the department supported an initial effort to update the Conscription Regulation for Curaçao and several appointments were made in accordance with local decisions. A working group appointed by the Minister of General Affairs of Aruba, with representation from CZMCARIB, ARUMIL, and officials from the Departamento Recurso Humano, made recommendations to adjust the appointment of the ARUMIL aimed at ‘per-

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.34)
sections.text: Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Area performance, motivation, and retention. The year concluded with an investigation into embedding and implementing the work responsibility that CZMCARIB partially holds over Caribbean personnel. The line responsibilities are nearly aligned with the responsibilities of defense personnel. Further decision-making regarding the status of CARMIL will receive the highest priority in the coming year. Safety and Environment Staff Officer: Captain (kaptmarns) R. van der Pol. A pair of reports from the Dutch Safety Board indicated that inadequate safety, i.e., the failure to organize a safe workplace, was the cause of two fatal accidents within defense. This did not go unnoticed at CZMCARIB either. This is evidenced by the decision to organize, in addition to the Safety Council CZMCARIB, which meets four times a year, a specific Theme Safety Council for Incidents biannually. This specific Council is entirely focused on the station ship Zr.Ms. Van Amstel in Curaçao.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.35)
sections.text: 7_KM_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-35 220 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean focused on learning from incidents. Additionally, it was assessed to what extent commanders and department heads actually implemented the established improvement measures. This gave learning from incidents a visible place within the CZMCARIB organization. Thus, structural attention was created for areas of improvement. Within the CZMCARIB Staff, the emphasis was on compliance with (Dutch and international) laws and regulations, implementing defense policy, support, and an assessment of hazardous materials in preparation for the deployment during Hurricane Irma, as well as inventorying operational risks and employing a (third-year HBO) intern to support commanders and department heads. Furthermore, several meetings took place with various ministries of the country of Curaçao. These meetings consistently addressed the lack of an installation capable of processing chemical waste in a responsible manner. At MBPAR, the focus was on two specific areas. Firstly, a new emergency response organization was established, and the emergency response plan and the Business Emergency Plan were completed in draft form. Additionally, MBPAR functioned as a waste collection point for other defense locations in the Caribbean. From here, Zr.Ms. Karel Doorman transported the collected chemical waste in four 20-foot containers and 10 pallets to the Netherlands. This waste was subsequently processed through the established structure there. MKSUF made significant progress in the area of safety and security regarding the storage of hazardous materials and munitions. Furthermore, 2017 was characterized for MKSUF by ongoing delays concerning the asbestos remediation of the obstacle course and the training location 'Operations in Urban Areas'. As a result, both training facilities have not been used for more than two and a half years, which heavily impacts operational output (training). On Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, safety awareness, controlling legionella, and the safe transport of hazardous materials were important safety and security topics. Additionally, in the last period of 2017, work began on updating the Risk Inventory and Risk Evaluation (RI&E). For the Sint Maarten detachment, it was working on resolving the issues identified by the Corps of Hazardous Materials Inspectors. In this context, a container for hazardous materials was placed that complies with Dutch PGS-15 regulations. Due to Hurricane Irma, the drafting of an RI&E for Detachment SXM was stalled. The hurricane also had an impact on

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.36)
sections.text:
Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied focused on the necessary refresher courses for company emergency responders (BHV’ers), which had rendered them outdated. MSKSAV aimed, among other things, to address the training backlog. Thus, 34 employees at MSKSAV completed the Company Emergency Response training. Additionally, V&M consultations were established at the level of the workshops. Furthermore, supervision over the use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) was intensified, such as monitoring the wearing of protective clothing, eye and face protection, and hearing protection devices. In relation to the environment, MSKSAV established collection points. In this way, different types of waste (wood, scrap metal, paper, fluorescent tubes, and residual waste) are collected separately. 

Company Social Work (BMW) region CARIB Head: Lieutenant Commander (ltz1) H.J.H. Goetzee. The main tasks performed by Company Social Work (BMW) in the Caribbean region are assistance, services, reporting, support after traumatic events, and crisis intervention. For the CARIB region, BMW, together with Spiritual Care (GV), is responsible for notifying family members. BMW is available 24/7 for personnel and their families. Since June 1, BMW has been part of the Personnel Care Service Center (DC PZ) of the Defense Support Command. In 2017, BMW provided psychosocial assistance to employees and their families throughout the CARIB region. Unlike the regional offices in the Netherlands, there is often a need for long-term assistance in the Caribbean region. This is partly due to the unique situation of overseas placements and the inability to rely on alternatives such as General Social Work or other forms of civil assistance. In 2017, the department regularly conducted work visits to Bonaire, where the Royal Marechaussee (KMAR) is active, and to Sint Maarten, in order to be more accessible to personnel and their families on these islands.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.37)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean In the context of providing services to commanders, information and advisory reports have been prepared, and participation has taken place in the Social Medical Team of CZMCARIB and the Royal Marechaussee. Due to Hurricane Irma, there was a significant demand for the deployment of the BMW personnel from BMW CARIB starting in September. An additional BMW member supported from the Netherlands for several weeks. This year, BMW also focused on the initiative to better address issues related to relational violence. The department held an informational session for several teachers from local schools where many children of defense personnel are placed. The goal of this collaboration is to recognize signals at an earlier stage and provide support if necessary. In doing so, we adhere to the official guidelines provided by Dutch law and the Professional Association of Social Work Professionals. BMW was also involved in local veteran care. In Curaçao, the Veterans Care first meeting was held in Sint Maarten to coordinate assistance.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.38)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean and the Curaçao Veterans Association is active and represents the interests of veterans residing on the island. BMW established contact with this association to provide access for veterans living in Curaçao from the position as a partner within the National Care System for Veterans. In this context, there are also contacts with the Veterans Care Desk of the ABP in the Netherlands. Additionally, there are contacts with caregivers from the local Mental Health Care. Spiritual Care Chaplain: P. Vlaar (Aruba) Chaplain: F. van Grimbergen (Curaçao) Pastor: J. Wójcik (Curaçao) Humanistic Counselor: N. de Kooter The spiritual caregivers go wherever the men and women of Defense go. In the Caribbean, this also applies to partners, families with children, and veterans. Every first Saturday of the month, a spiritual caregiver can be found with a number of veterans at the military cemetery on Roodeweg, where they carry out minor maintenance. On May 4, the annual Memorial Day took place there. A spiritual caregiver also delivered a short reflection during the commemoration at the monument at Waaigat. On the last Thursday of May, there was a memorial moment at the Parera naval base for all military personnel of the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM) who have passed away. The Ascencion Country House is one of the objects of Monument Care Curaçao. Therefore, this residence is always open to the public on the first Sunday of the month. This open day starts with an ecumenical church service of word and prayer in the chapel of the Ascencion Country House, led by the chaplain or pastor. The audience consists of military personnel and their families, veterans, local people, tourists, and guests. After the service, people can meet each other in a relaxed atmosphere while enjoying snacks and drinks. There is music, stalls with books, jewelry, souvenirs, art, driftwood, etc. And there is an opportunity to participate in a guided tour of the estate with information about the history of the Country House. The open house and church services are well attended throughout the year.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.39)
sections.text:
Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied

Additionally, formation days are regularly held by the chaplains. This year, the stationed military personnel of the CIDW were welcomed and introduced to the island of Curaçao. The military personnel working on the station ship were also given the opportunity to participate in a formation day together. The CURMIL enjoyed several training days on Ascension, as did the EMV, PO-TOC trainees, and the students of the police and coast guard training. In May, a FLO conference took place. Over three days, the Chaplaincy Service reflected on the past, present, and future. Normally, military personnel attend the FLO conference in Beukbergen in the Netherlands, but not everyone was able to do so. Furthermore, a number of FLO participants reside in Curaçao. Therefore, this tailored conference for military personnel and their partners was offered locally. Landhuis Ascension is a place where people like to go for meetings, team-building sessions, or gatherings. It is also frequently used as a training location. Dutch and foreign units regularly set up a command post there in 2017 and transformed the parking lot and the immediate surroundings of the landhuis into a bivouac site with tents, trucks, and communication equipment. After the deployment of military personnel to Sint Maarten, debriefing meetings were held on Ascension to reflect on this special task together. In December, the traditional Christmas market took place, and a pleasant and well-catered veterans' dinner was organized.

Sint Maarten

The Royal Marechaussee has over 150 personnel working on various islands in the Caribbean. Therefore, the humanist counselor regularly travels to the Windward Islands and Bonaire to visit the personnel there. He can also be found at the Marechaussee brigade in Suffisant. 2017 will go down in history as the year when Irma ravaged Sint Maarten. Immediately after the storm, the chaplaincy was present on the island to assist affected military personnel and families. In September and October, many military personnel were deployed to Sint Maarten. The chaplaincy was also present for them, even providing stroopwafels during church services or reflection services. In Aruba and Curaçao, the evacuated families were supported, and the chaplaincy assisted colleagues with the intensive work.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.40)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Celebrations From May 16 to 28, ten ladies from this choir traveled to Lourdes. In total, there was a delegation from Aruba and Curaçao of 41 participants who joined the Dutch delegation and took part in the impressive pilgrimage. Some flew for the first time, seeing snow in the Pyrenees for the first time in their lives. All had an indescribable experience in the southern French town, where approximately 20,000 soldiers from 35 different countries met each other. Traditionally, the spiritual care organized the Christmas Eve celebration on December 24. Over 800 people came to the parade ground of the naval base Parera that evening to celebrate this beautiful event together. The children's choir Angelitos and the Sranan Rosoes provided the musical entertainment, and there was poeroet and kerststol. The spiritual caregivers, together with the soldiers of the naval base Parera, contributed to a traditional and unifying celebration. The engineers of CIDW 26 built a new nativity scene for this celebration. Country House Ascencion. (Source: Wikimedia)

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.41)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Force in the Caribbean Area Spiritual caregivers also participated in exercises. Exercises of the CIDW were faithfully attended, as well as those of CURMIL. The spiritual caregiver from Aruba participated in exercises such as the MOUT in the United States. On board Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, spiritual care was regularly present. Moreover, they frequently visited the various units; whether they were active at Parera or Suffisant, with the Coast Guard or with the brigade of the Marechaussee. In 2017, they participated in various events: Ride for the Roses, sports days, all hands, solidarity meals, barracks meetings, receptions, introduction days for newly assigned personnel, notification services, OPS briefings, Social-Medical Consultations, veterans' café, crisis interventions, KLM marathon, good causes committee, MSV, hospital visits at SEHOS, etc. Defense Materiel Organization/Joint Information Provision Command (DMO/JIVC) Team Leader: Lieutenant (ltz2) T. van der Wereld During the first half of the year, an inventory was conducted in preparation for the transfer of various ICT services (internet and telephony) from the CZSK organization to DMO/JIVC. In the second half of 2017, testing of the equipment to be used in the future began. A prerequisite for connecting the Marine detachment in Sint Maarten to the defense network was the dismantling of a microwave link and connecting the location to the fiber optic network of a local provider. This was accomplished in the third quarter of 2017. In the last quarter of the year, preparations began for adjusting the local passive infrastructure at MB Parera (fiber optic network) for the expansion of internet services and modernization of the WiFi internet network in the barracks accommodations.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.42)
sections.text: Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Medical Service CZMCARIB Head: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) C. Spaargaren Practice Manager: Lieutenant (ltz2) M.S. Boot In addition to primary care, the Medical Service provided operational support to local and external units at the Wacawa training area. This included shooting exercises, diving exercises, sniper training, camping, marches, climbing, cycling, and running. Additionally, training was conducted outside of Curaçao, such as HUREX, MOUT, and jungle training. In the first week of September, Hurricane Irma swept over the Leeward Islands. With a doctor and six Medical Assistants (AMV) on Sint Maarten, one AMV on Saba, one AMV on St Eustatius, one AMV on Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, and a medical advisor with a medical staff officer in Curaçao, a large deployment occurred. Furthermore, a trauma doctor, a staff doctor, a BME, and two evacuation teams along with a HPG member were flown in from the Netherlands to support and ultimately relieve the EGB personnel. Soldiers practice administering an intravenous line in Curaçao.

sections.title: Commandement Der Zeemacht Carib (p.43)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean In April, exactly one year after the establishment of the EGB, the evaluation period ended and it was time to take stock. Despite the need for some minor adjustments, the EGB is performing well. By the end of the year, this had resulted in the awarding of a civil quality certificate (HKZ). The Medical Service is also innovating in operational areas. Following the deployment in Sint Maarten, it adapted its own emergency aid package. The materials that the Service needs during such a mission are now more flexible to deploy and better equipped for the type of assistance it must provide. The personnel are also enthusiastic about integrating with the operational units to improve collaboration and increase mutual awareness between both parties. Defense Security and Safety Organization (DBBO) Head: Mr. M.J.T. Hoek, from July 15 Mr. R.L. Bröker Access Control The department has adjusted the access control. In addition, it worked hard on the implementation regulations regarding the admission of suppliers. Patrol and Intervention DBBO conducted patrols and interventions together with the CUR and ARUMIL (blue platoon) to protect the interests of Defense. In addition to these main tasks, it also carried out the first response task, which is managed from the central control room at MBPAR. Training, Certification, and Education This year, the personnel received further training in their IBT skills to perform the above tasks even better. Various courses were also attended, such as APK II and APK III. Work Visits The following work visits took place from the Netherlands: C-DBBO together with C-BEV region West DBBO and SR P&O AIFB DBBO PM DBBO and Aost DV&B.

Rudolph New Year's Receptions At the beginning of the year, New Year's receptions take place at many locations. This year at the KIM, there was the New Year's reception of C-ZSK and, as usual, the New Year's reception of the KIM and the Faculty of Military Sciences. Senate Transition January is also the month of the senate transition. The Senate is the governing body of the Corps of Cadets. This year we said goodbye to the 113th Senate during the inauguration of the 114th Senate. Presentation Submarine Service for Cadets Within the organization, there were also promotion rounds to excite cadets at the KIM for the Submarine Service. This year, the staff of this service held a presentation at the KIM for the cadets of the sea service.

sections.title: Bijlagen Colofon 19 12 2022 (p.3)
sections.text: KIM Cross - 50th Edition Under ideal weather conditions, the 50th edition of the KIM Cross took place on February 27. The start was at the soccer field of the Helder soccer club in Den Helder. Participants covered either 4 km or 8 km via paved paths, riding trails, and on the beach. For the cadets, participation was mandatory, but for many defense participants, it has become a baseline measurement for assessing their fitness level. Commemoration of the Battle of the Java Sea "All ships follow me!" Thus spoke Rear Admiral Karel Doorman. Near the bust of Doorman, in the garden of the KIM, the Battle of the Java Sea was also commemorated on February 27, which took place on that date in 1942 between an Allied task force under his command and the Imperial Japanese Navy under Rear Admiral Takeo Takagi. The Combined Striking Force of 14 Dutch, American, British, and Australian ships was defeated. The blow was particularly hard for the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM). In addition to Doorman, over 900 KM personnel lost their lives in the waters of Indonesia. KIM Cross 2017.

sections.title: Bijlagen Colofon 19 12 2022 (p.4)
sections.text: Attachments Working Visit of C-ZSK to the Corps of Cadets Almost annually, C-ZSK pays a working visit to the Corps of Cadets. These sessions typically take place informally in 't Zaaltje, the living room of the KIM. C-ZSK inquires about the well-being of the cadets, and the cadets question the flag officer on various topics. Annual Competitions From first-year to senior cadets, everyone participates. Because everyone strives for their year to come out on top. From volleyball to soccer. At the end of the day, the best always wins, and this is celebrated with cakes. Not too many, as the participants concluded the day with a dinner. Paresto provided the dinner in the company restaurant 't Oppertje. Working visit of C-ZSK to the Corps of Cadets.

sections.title: Bijlagen Colofon 19 12 2022 (p.6)
sections.text: Defense Simulation Symposium The second Defense Simulation Symposium took place this year at the ship handling simulator of the KIM. During the symposium, an interested audience listened to presentations from key players in the field, various workshops were held, and among others, cadets participated in demonstrations. Furthermore, there was ample opportunity to experience the latest maritime simulators firsthand. This year, the focus of the symposium was on maritime operations. The previous Defense Simulation Symposium highlighted land operations, and at a future event, the focus will be on air operations. The symposium was intended for all defense personnel involved in simulation systems as part of the Training and Education within the Readiness Process. Guest Lecture by the Royal Netherlands Marine Corps Band For the first time, the Marine Corps Band provided a guest lecture for the Corps of Cadets. "When is it appropriate to applaud? How do you know when a piece is finished?" By now, a large group of cadets knows the answers to these questions. The following evening, they were able to put their learning into practice in the presence of their parents. The Marine Corps Band held a concert at the theater de Kampanje for the entire Corps of Cadets, their parents, and the staff of the KIM. Dies Natalis (Birthday of the KIM) Annually, the KIM celebrates the anniversary (April 25, 1829) of the Institute. This year featured presentations by Captain (TD) ir. A.L. Vergroesen (MTPS, the technological master of the NLDA), Ing. C.A. Scheele (Astronomical navigation in Newton's spacetime - Past and present of astronomical navigation), and Dr. A.J. van der Wal (Astronomical navigation in Einstein's spacetime - Future of astronomical navigation). An interesting start to the morning included a solo musical interlude by one of the cadets on violin. Change of Command Commandant KIM Following the Dies Natalis, the Change of Command for the Commandant KIM took place. The now-promoted Commodore P. van den Berg handed over the flag of the Corps of Cadets to Captain (ktz) J.C. de Bruijn. SAIL Den Helder 2017 was the year of SAIL Den Helder, which also took place in and around the KIM grounds. The captains' dinner was held at the KIM, and the cadets participated in the crew parade.

sections.title: Bijlagen Colofon 19 12 2022 (p.7)
sections.text: Great River Race In the first weekend of September, the Great River Race took place in London. Each year, a rowing team of cadets participates in this gigantic monster race. For approximately three hours, they row continuously along the River Thames. The results were commendable. This year, the team also finished in the top ranks. Ceremonial At various occasions, such as Prinsjesdag, the Commando transfer of the CZSK, Remembrance Day, etc., the CZSK organization calls upon the presence of (a delegation of) the Corps of Cadets multiple times. Installation Promotion 2017 In the presence of their parents, staff from the KIM and the FMW, and alumni from 50 years ago, around one hundred cadets were installed this year as well. Promotion 2017 began in early September at the KIM, after which they underwent the maritime introduction period at MKERF, Texel, and on board Zr.Ms. Rotterdam. The installation was the concluding event, after which they could return home for the first time. The Monday after the installation, the cadets departed for the Marines to the Van Ghent Barracks to follow the Practical Training to Officer of the Marines. The remaining cadets began their classes at the KIM. Assaut 2017 The Assaut is the gala ball of the Corps of Cadets, which is part of the cadets' curriculum. From start to finish, this celebration is organized by the cadets, and the KIM undergoes a true metamorphosis. This year's theme was: 'Once upon a time in the West'. Coast Guard Netherlands Captain (ktz) R.J. Blok MSc In 2017, the Coast Guard made several important decisions regarding the modernization of the organization as well as the manner in which it carried out regular Coast Guard tasks in the areas of service and enforcement. The (political) decision-making regarding the new MOC to be developed was completed on December 7 with the discussion of the letter to the House, formally launching the project.

sections.title: Bijlagen Colofon 19 12 2022 (p.8)
sections.text: This decision-making process is an important step towards a modern and future-oriented Coast Guard that operates information-driven and is equipped for its tasks. Furthermore, steps have been taken in the development of the operational resources through the elaboration of the operational concept "Interception from a ship." An important step in this is the commencement of an acclimatization period for information-driven deployment of an enforcement team consisting of police, customs, and the Royal Marechaussee (Koninklijke Marechaussee). Preparations for the acquisition of two Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPV) including interceptors, to replace the existing ships, have started in close cooperation with the Rijksrederij. An investigation into the formation of the Coast Guard in relation to its current tasks and modernization led to a principle approval for the expansion of the Coast Guard's formation by 23 FTEs. The implementation of this expansion will take place in the coming years through a reorganization process. Flag Coast Guard.
